D.t: Hallie Shoffner trails by 10.4 and wins 5% of simulations. Closing it takes about 50,937 voters switching sides, or 101,873 more net votes from new turnout.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between R +17.7 and R +2.8. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.
The polls page average is R +9.7. Your best recent poll is GrayHouse (R) at R +8.6; your worst is Hendrix College at R +10.4. 2 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Pulaski, a projected net 52,362 votes; Washington, a projected net 11,138 votes; Jefferson, a projected net 7,141 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Benton, R +11.0, 10.3% of the vote; Faulkner, R +10.8, 4.5% of the vote; Mississippi, R +3.0, 0.9% of the vote; Ouachita, D +3.4, 0.7% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Hallie Shoffner runs furthest behind in Benton, Baxter, Pulaski. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 65% of voters, 40 to 57, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.23 points; Voters without a degree, 61% of voters, 41 to 56, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.06 points; Voters who find daily costs hard to afford, 60% of voters, 48 to 48, where a 5 point gain is worth 2.98 points.
The forecast's worst groups for Hallie Shoffner: Immigration voters 19 to 78, White voters 32 to 64, Small counties 33 to 64. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
